problem:
Which of the following augmented matrices are in row echelon form?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & -7 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 5\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & 0 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

feedback.problem:
Which of the following augmented matrices are in row echelon form?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}],\,\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 11\end{aligned}],\,\,C=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 6 & 8 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Remember that an augmented matrix is in row echelon form if its coefficient matrix satisfies the following conditions:

- All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the bottom of the matrix.
- Each leading entry of a row is in a column to the right of the leading entry of the row above it.

With that in mind, let's look at each matrix in turn.

- The matrix $A$ is not in row echelon form since ${a}_{32}\ne 0$ (condition II is violated). 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ is not in row echelon form since the first row contains only zeros and it is not at the bottom of the matrix (condition I is violated).

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 11\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $C$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 6 & 8 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, only $C$ is in row echelon form.
